PR title:
Accept valid unicode identifiers as class parameter to make_class

PR body:
Related to #1404



Gold patch (use only to infer the symptom; do not quote or describe the fix):
diff --git a/changelog.d/1406.change.md b/changelog.d/1406.change.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..4eae78ac
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog.d/1406.change.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+`attrs.make_class()` now allows for Unicode class names.
diff --git a/src/attr/_make.py b/src/attr/_make.py
index e3e31ffc..a7a4075a 100644
--- a/src/attr/_make.py
+++ b/src/attr/_make.py
@@ -13,6 +13,7 @@ import linecache
 import sys
 import types
 import typing
+import unicodedata
 
 from operator import itemgetter
 
@@ -2907,7 +2908,11 @@ def make_class(
     .. versionadded:: 17.1.0 *bases*
     .. versionchanged:: 18.1.0 If *attrs* is ordered, the order is retained.
     .. versionchanged:: 23.2.0 *class_body*
+    .. versionchanged:: 25.2.0 Class names can now be unicode.
     """
+    # Class identifiers are converted into the normal form NFKC while parsing
+    name = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", name)
+

message.content: `attrs.make_class()` rejects class names that contain valid Unicode characters, even though Python itself supports such identifiers.
